reasons: Both order internet and furniture in time and are well structured in Russian by week. A plans the 4-hour server window with backup, restore tests, a startup checklist and an explicit fallback if the server does not come up, while B has no rollback plan and tells IT to stop services on Friday 20 November, which contradicts the 4-hour downtime limit. B also gives 6 November as the furniture deadline (it is actually 13 November) and writes 'аптайм' where it means downtime; A has smaller date slips.

A: States furniture ordered Tue 3 Nov arrives by Fri 20 Nov; 5 working days from 3 Nov is about 10 Nov.
On Mon 16 Nov says internet is at day 6 of 10, inconsistent with an order placed on 2 Nov.
B: Presents 6 Nov as the furniture order deadline; with 5 working days the real deadline is 13 Nov.
Stopping server services on Fri 20 Nov conflicts with the 4-hour downtime window on 22 Nov.
Labels the 4-hour limit as server 'uptime' instead of downtime.
